**PUBLIC NOTICE – OFFICIAL LAUNCH OF THE COMMUNITY HEALTH OUTREACH PROGRAM (CHOP)**

The Rivers State Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the Partnership for Community Action on Primary Care, is pleased to announce the official launch of the Community Health Outreach Program (CHOP). The program is designed to strengthen community-level primary healthcare delivery, improve maternal and child health outcomes, and expand access to health education and preventive services across the 23 local government areas of Rivers State.

**1. Program Commencement**

The Community Health Outreach Program start_date is 2019-06-01, as announced in the launch notice. Record status: current. All program activities, including facility registration, community health education sessions, and mobile outreach clinics, will commence on this date. This launch marks the formal beginning of a multi-year initiative funded jointly by the State Government and the Global Health Partnership Trust.

**2. Program Objectives**

The core objectives of CHOP are as follows:

a) To reduce maternal and infant mortality rates in rural and peri-urban communities by at least 25 percent over the next five years;

b) To increase the number of pregnant women attending at least four antenatal care visits from the current baseline of 58 percent to 75 percent by December 2023;

c) To provide free basic health screening services (blood pressure, blood glucose, malaria, and HIV testing) to an estimated 120,000 residents annually;

d) To train and deploy 500 community health extension workers (CHEWs) and 250 community health officers (CHOs) to underserved wards;

e) To establish functional community health committees in all 319 wards of the state by June 2021;

f) To promote health-seeking behavior through culturally appropriate health education campaigns in English, Pidgin, Ikwerre, Ijaw, and Ogoni.

**3. Operational Structure**

The program will operate under the following administrative structure:

- **Program Coordinator:** Dr. Adaeze Okafor (Ministry of Health)
- **Deputy Coordinator (Operations):** Pharm. Ibrahim Suleiman
- **Deputy Coordinator (Community Engagement):** Mrs. Blessing Amadi
- **State Program Office:** CHOP Headquarters, Plot 14, Unity Road, GRA Phase II, Port Harcourt
- **Zonal Offices:** Three zonal offices will be established in Port Harcourt (Rivers East), Ahoada (Rivers West), and Degema (Rivers Central) to coordinate field activities.

**4. Registration of Health Facilities**

All primary healthcare centers, private clinics, and maternity homes wishing to participate in the program must complete the following steps:

i. Obtain a registration form from any CHOP zonal office or download from the program website (www.chop-rivers.org.ng/registration);

ii. Submit the completed form along with a copy of the facility's current license from the Rivers State Hospitals Management Board;

iii. Undergo a verification visit by a CHOP monitoring team;

iv. Receive a CHOP facility identification number and participation certificate.

Registration opens on 1 June 2019 and closes on 31 August 2019. Late applications will be considered only in exceptional circumstances and must be accompanied by a written justification.

**5. Community Health Education Campaigns**

As part of the launch activities, CHOP will conduct community health education sessions in the following pilot communities during the month of June 2019:

**Subject:** Establishment of the Mainland Outreach Unit and Update on Program Activities

The Community Health Outreach Program (CHOP) wishes to inform all stakeholders, participating health facilities, community health committees, and the general public of the following developments.

**1. Establishment of the Mainland Outreach Unit**

Following the successful completion of the pilot phase and the assessment of service delivery gaps in the riverine and mainland areas of the state, the Program Management Office has approved the establishment of a dedicated unit to coordinate outreach activities in the mainland corridor. The Mainland Outreach Unit was established on 2020-02-10 per the organizational chart. Record status: current. This unit will serve as the coordinating hub for all CHOP field operations in the mainland local government areas, working alongside the existing zonal offices.

The new unit will be responsible for the following:

i. Coordinating the deployment of mobile health teams to hard-to-reach communities in the mainland axis;
ii. Liaising with local government health departments and traditional institutions to facilitate community entry;
iii. Managing the distribution of health commodities and consumables to outreach sites;
iv. Collating field reports and ensuring timely submission to the State Program Office;
v. Supervising community health extension workers (CHEWs) and community health officers (CHOs) assigned to mainland wards.

The Mainland Outreach Unit will operate from a temporary office within the Port Harcourt Zonal Office until a permanent location is identified. Operational details, including contact lines and staff deployment, will be communicated in a subsequent announcement.

**2. Update on Health Facility Registration**

As of 31 January 2020, a total of 214 primary healthcare centers, 67 private clinics, and 23 maternity homes have successfully completed their registration with CHOP and have received their facility identification numbers. **8. Community Health Outreach Program – First Quarter 2020 Progress Report**

The Program Management Office is pleased to present the progress report for the first quarter of 2020. The report covers the period 1 January to 31 March 2020 and highlights key achievements, challenges, and planned activities for the second quarter.

**Overview of Activities**

During the first quarter, the program conducted a total of 24 outreach sessions across the three zones. These sessions focused on maternal health, child nutrition, immunization, and family planning. A total of 1,847 individuals participated in the sessions, exceeding the target of 1,500 participants set for the quarter.

**Key Achievements**

- **Community Health Education Sessions:** 24 sessions were held in 18 communities. The most well-attended sessions were those focused on immunization, with an average attendance of 112 participants per session.
- **Health Facility Registration:** Verification visits for the first cohort of facilities were completed in January. A total of 36 facilities were verified and registered. The second cohort verification visits commenced on 10 February as planned, and the teams have so far completed visits to 29 of the 45 facilities scheduled for the quarter.
- **Community Mobilization:** A total of 62 community mobilizers were trained and deployed across the program areas. The mobilizers conducted door-to-door sensitization in preparation for the education sessions.
- **Partnerships:** The program established new partnerships with three local non-governmental organizations to support the distribution of insecticide-treated nets and the promotion of exclusive breastfeeding.

**Challenges**

- **Inclement Weather:** Heavy rainfall in March affected access to some communities in the North zone, leading to the postponement of two sessions. These sessions have been rescheduled for April.
- **Transportation Costs:** The cost of transportation to remote communities was higher than budgeted, resulting in a 12% overrun on the transportation line item. The Program Management Office is reviewing the budget to address this variance.

**Planned Activities for the Second Quarter**

- Continuation of community health education sessions as per the revised schedule.
- Completion of the second cohort facility verification visits.
- Launch of the community health fair scheduled for May.
- Distribution of insecticide-treated nets in collaboration with partner organizations.

The full progress report is available for review at the Program Management Office and will be shared with all stakeholders at the next quarterly review meeting.

TO ALL HEALTH FACILITIES, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND RESIDENTS OF RIVERS STATE

**PUBLIC NOTICE – OFFICIAL LAUNCH OF THE COMMUNITY HEALTH OUTREACH PROGRAM (CHOP)**

The Rivers State Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the Partnership for Community Action on Primary Care, is pleased to announce the official launch of the Community Health Outreach Program (CHOP). The program is designed to strengthen community-level primary healthcare delivery, improve maternal and child health outcomes, and expand access to health education and preventive services across the 23 local government areas of Rivers State.

**1. Program Commencement**

The Community Health Outreach Program start_date is 2019-06-01, as announced in the launch notice. Record status: current. All program activities, including facility registration, community health education sessions, and mobile outreach clinics, will commence on this date. This launch marks the formal beginning of a multi-year initiative funded jointly by the State Government and the Global Health Partnership Trust.

**2. Program Objectives**

The core objectives of CHOP are as follows:

a) To reduce maternal and infant mortality rates in rural and peri-urban communities by at least 25 percent over the next five years;

b) To increase the number of pregnant women attending at least four antenatal care visits from the current baseline of 58 percent to 75 percent by December 2023;

c) To provide free basic health screening services (blood pressure, blood glucose, malaria, and HIV testing) to an estimated 120,000 residents annually;

d) To train and deploy 500 community health extension workers (CHEWs) and 250 community health officers (CHOs) to underserved wards;

e) To establish functional community health committees in all 319 wards of the state by June 2021;

f) To promote health-seeking behavior through culturally appropriate health education campaigns in English, Pidgin, Ikwerre, Ijaw, and Ogoni.

**3. Operational Structure**

The program will operate under the following administrative structure:

**8. Community Health Outreach Program – First Quarter 2020 Progress Report**

The Program Management Office is pleased to present the progress report for the first quarter of 2020. The report covers the period 1 January to 31 March 2020 and highlights key achievements, challenges, and planned activities for the second quarter.

**Overview of Activities**

During the first quarter, the program conducted a total of 24 outreach sessions across the three zones. These sessions focused on maternal health, child nutrition, immunization, and family planning. A total of 1,847 individuals participated in the sessions, exceeding the target of 1,500 participants set for the quarter.

**Key Achievements**

- **Community Health Education Sessions:** 24 sessions were held in 18 communities. The most well-attended sessions were those focused on immunization, with an average attendance of 112 participants per session.
- **Health Facility Registration:** Verification visits for the first cohort of facilities were completed in January. A total of 36 facilities were verified and registered. The second cohort verification visits commenced on 10 February as planned, and the teams have so far completed visits to 29 of the 45 facilities scheduled for the quarter.
- **Community Mobilization:** A total of 62 community mobilizers were trained and deployed across the program areas. The mobilizers conducted door-to-door sensitization in preparation for the education sessions.
- **Partnerships:** The program established new partnerships with three local non-governmental organizations to support the distribution of insecticide-treated nets and the promotion of exclusive breastfeeding.

**Challenges**

- **Inclement Weather:** Heavy rainfall in March affected access to some communities in the North zone, leading to the postponement of two sessions. These sessions have been rescheduled for April.
- **Transportation Costs:** The cost of transportation to remote communities was higher than budgeted, resulting in a 12% overrun on the transportation line item. The Program Management Office is reviewing the budget to address this variance.

**Planned Activities for the Second Quarter**

- Continuation of community health education sessions as per the revised schedule.
- Completion of the second cohort facility verification visits.
- Launch of the community health fair scheduled for May.
- Distribution of insecticide-treated nets in collaboration with partner organizations.

The full progress report is available for review at the Program Management Office and will be shared with all stakeholders at the next quarterly review meeting.
